prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system produces compliant potable water; boundary: River Intake Pump Station (Ironwood) through Raw Water Screen Channel/treatment/storage to High Service Pump Header; distribution excluded.

Ironwood normally automatic, withdrawal-limited. Chief Operator authorizes Storm Intake Mode/manual operation; manual requires understood cause, observable equipment, acceptable continuity risk. Permissives: suction/discharge availability, healthy motor, open isolation, no trips; downstream low level, drive fault, local control, unproven interlock block starts; losses alarm/stop by severity. Raw Water Screen Channel monitors levels/differential/debris/rake; sends Rake Torque Snapshot each cleaning cycle; high-high requires immediate field confirmation. Storms intensify observation/testing. Normal return requires river level, differential, quality, cycling stabilized for Chief Operator-approved duration. Maintenance Planner schedules poststorm inspections/cleaning.

Chief Operator establishes coagulant dose using turbidity/color/alkalinity/pH/temperature/bench observations. Coagulant Dosing Skid (Marigold) automatically meters primary coagulant; sends Alum Batch Ticket for new lots. Trimming requires analyzer feedback, operator targets, verified response—not one instrument. Duty Engineer may authorize temporary rapid-turbidity adjustments; Chief Operator confirms sustained setpoint. Poststorm coagulation/filtration normalizes only with stable-feed/predictable-loading trends.

North Filter Gallery (Cobalt): gravity filters; records individual effluent turbidity/headloss each scan. South Filter Gallery sends Filter Run Exception Note for abnormal endings. Run management considers duration/headloss/turbidity/backwash/upstream condition. Return requires rinse-to-waste target and stable turbidity; unusual rises require sample comparison. Laboratory Technician confirms discrepancies/abnormalities; Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench receives process/compliance samples.

Chlorine Contact Basin: Chlorine Residual Alarm requires immediate assessment. Clearwell Level Controller buffers restrictions; Backwash Recovery Tank supports recovery. Distribution Dispatcher receives demand-risk notifications; North Distribution Pressure Station/South Distribution Pressure Station influence pumping. SCADA Historian Server (Lantern) retains trends; controls share time. Duty Engineer governs changes; Chemical Supplier Driver follows delivery/inventory checks; Residuals Hauler removes residuals/backwash. Trained staff supervise/document.

Document units:
S066: The Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench is used for custody-controlled receipt of compliance and process samples collected from treatment locations.
S067: The SCADA Historian Server retains dose changes, analyzer values, filter status changes, wash sequences, and operator comments for later review.
S068: Manual override is permitted for chemical feed, valve sequencing, and filter start or stop actions only when automatic control is unavailable or inappropriate for the condition.
S069: An operator placing equipment in manual control is expected to state the reason, monitor the affected process variable closely, and restore automatic control as soon as practicable.
S070: Manual chemical feed changes are made in small increments unless an immediate water-quality risk requires a larger correction approved by the Chief Operator.
S071: If analyzer feedback is lost, operating staff hold the last verified safe dose or revert to an approved fixed dose while collecting additional grab samples.
S072: A sustained loss of coagulation effectiveness is treated as a process deviation and prompts review of chemical strength, feed pump status, mixing energy, and raw-water characteristics.
S073: The Chlorine Contact Basin is considered in the response because excessive particulate carryover can affect downstream disinfectant demand and contact performance.
S074: The Clearwell Level Controller remains coordinated with filter production so that filter shutdowns, backwashes, and return-to-service decisions do not create avoidable storage swings.
S075: When filter capacity is reduced, the Distribution Dispatcher is advised of expected production limits before changes affect the High Service Pump Header.
S076: After any significant deviation, the Chief Operator reviews trends from the affected operating period and confirms that corrective actions restored stable clarified and filtered water quality.
S077: Following operating deviations, laboratory sampling provides independent confirmation that treatment targets have returned to acceptable control ranges.
S078: The Chief Operator establishes daily sampling priorities based on plant conditions, regulatory monitoring requirements, and recent process adjustments.
S079: The Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench is also known as Sparrow for local bench labeling during sample receipt.
S080: Field samples are labeled at collection with location, time, collector initials, preservation method, and requested analyses before they leave operating areas.
S081: The Laboratory Technician checks container type, holding time, temperature, preservative status, and seal condition before logging a sample for analysis.
S082: Samples from the River Intake Pump Station, Raw Water Screen Channel, North Filter Gallery, South Filter Gallery, Chlorine Contact Basin, and High Service Pump Header are verified against the current sampling schedule before testing begins.
